item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-d886e5b208764c0a","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"The government continued systematically detaining and prosecuting peaceful critics and activists, often equating peaceful dissent with terrorism; it detained and prosecuted protesters and activists in Palestine-solidarity demonstrations and detained family members and supporters of presidential hopeful Ahmed Tantawy. A national dialogue initiated by Sisi produced no recognizable policy reforms by October, while authorities continued arresting activists, including dialogue participants.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.8","4B.2","4B.3","4B.10","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Events and assessments during 2023; the national dialogue began in 2022 and its 2023 lack of reforms is directly reported.","ruler_attribution":"Human Rights Watch attributes the actions to Egyptian authorities and identifies the national dialogue as initiated by President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi; the source does not establish that Sisi personally ordered each detention.","limitations":["Human Rights Watch is a secondary advocacy source.","The report does not quantify all arrests or establish personal responsibility for every incident."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d886e5b208764c0a","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Between April 2022 and September 2023, authorities released roughly 1,700 unjustly detained prisoners, including Ahmed Douma, but a local rights campaign reported more than 4,500 arrests during the same period, including some people who had just been released.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.10","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The reported interval overlaps 2023 and ends in September 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The figures concern Egyptian authorities; no individual decision by Sisi is specified.","limitations":["The arrest figure is attributed to a local rights campaign and is not independently verified in the excerpt.","The interval begins before 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d886e5b208764c0a","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"Interior Ministry police and National Security agents continued forcibly disappearing critics and dissidents; detainees were frequently subjected to torture and forced confessions. Prison conditions remained dire, with denial of family and lawyer visits and inadequate medical care. Prosecutors refused a request to reopen the investigation into the disappearance, mistreatment, and suspicious death in custody of economist Aymad Hadhoud.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.9","4B.4","7B.2","7B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The source reports continuing conditions and a prosecutorial decision during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes conduct to Interior Ministry police, National Security agents, prison authorities, and prosecutors; it does not prove Sisi personally directed the abuses or refusal.","limitations":["The source does not provide a complete incident count.","Some described detention practices are ongoing or historical rather than newly initiated in 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d886e5b208764c0a","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"Egyptian security forces arbitrarily detained women and girls related to suspected Wilayat Sina' members in North Sinai during 2017–2022; 12 of 21 were held incommunicado for two weeks to six months, and relatives reported beatings and electric shocks. The US State Department added Egypt in September 2023 to its list of countries implicated in using child soldiers based on reports of military joint operations with allied militias that recruited children; a Sinai rights group reported recruitment of boys as young as 16, some of whom were injured or killed.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.5","2B.9","3B.1","3B.2","3B.7","3B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The child-soldier listing and documentation were reported in 2023; the arbitrary detention incidents occurred in 2017–2022.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes conduct to Egyptian security forces, the military, and allied militias; it does not establish Sisi's personal involvement.","limitations":["The underlying detention events predate 2023.","The child-soldier designation is based on independent reports summarized by HRW."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d886e5b208764c0a","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"Authorities used restrictive criminal laws to suppress expression; they detained and prosecuted dozens of protesters, cordoned off peaceful protests, and sometimes used batons, sticks, and water cannons to disperse them. Courts sentenced activist Mohamed Adel to four years for Facebook posts critical of the government and IMF, and sentenced publisher Hisham Kassem to six months and a fine for libel, slander, and broadly worded charges involving disturbance of authorities.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.1"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The arrests, dispersals, and court decisions occurred in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The conduct is attributed to Egyptian authorities, prosecutors, courts, and security forces; personal direction by Sisi is not established.","limitations":["The source reports HRW's characterization of the prosecutions as unlawful or abusive.","The excerpt does not provide a full denominator for protest arrests."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d886e5b208764c0a","start_unit":6,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"A 2019 Associations Law registration deadline allowed authorities to shut down and freeze the assets of unregistered groups and banned undefined political work. Human rights activists remained under travel bans and asset freezes, and an emergency state security court sentenced 29 rights activists to prison terms of five years to life after a mass trial involving reported enforced disappearances, denial of family visits, and inadequate legal access.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.4","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The registration deadline and 2023 prosecutions and restrictions were active during 2023; the law was enacted in 2019.","ruler_attribution":"The restrictions are attributed to Egyptian authorities and courts; the source does not establish Sisi's personal role in each case.","limitations":["The law predates the period.","The due-process findings are reported by HRW and Egyptian organizations."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d886e5b208764c0a","start_unit":7,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"Egyptian authorities systematically refused or failed to renew identity documents for dissidents, journalists, and human rights activists abroad, apparently pressuring them to return; authorities also detained the fathers of two Egyptian dissidents abroad in August and held them in pretrial detention before releasing them without trial.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.5","4B.3","4B.7","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report describes continuing practices and August–October 2023 detentions.","ruler_attribution":"The actions are attributed to Egyptian authorities; personal authorization by Sisi is not demonstrated.","limitations":["The motive is described as apparent rather than conclusively established.","The source does not identify the officials responsible."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d886e5b208764c0a","start_unit":7,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"Authorities widely deployed videoconference hearings for pretrial detention in 2023, allowing detention-renewal sessions to occur remotely from prisons under police custody and limiting detainees' ability to appear physically before judges or communicate privately with lawyers.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","4B.4","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The system was widely deployed during 2023, with the Supreme State Security Prosecution beginning remote renewal sessions in June.","ruler_attribution":"The practice is attributed to Egyptian authorities and the prosecution; no personal decision by Sisi is specified.","limitations":["The source gives no complete count of affected detainees.","The assessment that the system is inherently abusive is HRW's finding."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d886e5b208764c0a","start_unit":7,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"Egypt's annual inflation reached 39.7 percent in August 2023; a Bloomberg analysis identified Egypt as the second-most vulnerable country to a debt crisis. The IMF's $3 billion loan agreement expanded Takaful and Karama coverage and included transparency conditions for military-owned businesses, but currency devaluation reduced transfer adequacy and the first two reviews were postponed after the government failed to meet transparency criteria.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.5","5B.7","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"All quantitative and policy developments described concern 2023; the IMF agreement was published in January 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The policies concern the Egyptian government under Sisi; the excerpt does not assign individual responsibility for the delayed reviews.","limitations":["The debt vulnerability is an external analysis, not a realized debt crisis.","The source does not isolate causal responsibility for inflation or currency depreciation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d886e5b208764c0a","start_unit":7,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"The government reported that Takaful and Karama cash-transfer programs covered more than 5 million families, or 22 million people, by September 2023, but this represented only about one-third of families living in or near poverty and transfers were inadequate against reforms, inflation, and low baseline social spending.","question_ids":["5B.8","5B.9","6B.2","6B.3","6B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Coverage and adequacy findings are reported for September 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Coverage was reported by the Egyptian government; adequacy and poverty-incidence assessments are HRW's analysis.","limitations":["The government coverage figure is not independently verified in the excerpt.","The source does not provide a counterfactual welfare estimate."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d886e5b208764c0a","start_unit":7,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"From July through November 2023, the government imposed daily or semi-daily nationwide electricity cutbacks; cuts appeared longer in rural and impoverished areas, disrupting work, healthcare work, and access to water during high temperatures.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.8","5B.9","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The electricity restrictions occurred from July to November 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The measures are attributed to the Egyptian government; the source does not identify Sisi's direct role in operational scheduling.","limitations":["The source does not quantify outage duration by region.","The claim about unequal duration is phrased as an apparent pattern."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d886e5b208764c0a","start_unit":7,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"Personal data of more than 72,000 children were exposed online for at least eight months, including identity, contact, school, photograph, and passport or national-ID information, in a university-application process involving the Egyptian government and a private British company.","question_ids":["1B.9","3B.7","4B.9","6B.2","6B.8","8B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The exposure existed during 2023 and had lasted at least eight months when reported.","ruler_attribution":"The source identifies the Egyptian government and a private company as involved; it does not establish Sisi's personal knowledge or response.","limitations":["The excerpt does not describe any official investigation, remedy, or attribution of the security failure."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d886e5b208764c0a","start_unit":8,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"Male-guardianship policies continued to restrict women's mobility; under the Personal Status Law, a woman could be deemed disobedient and lose spousal maintenance if she left the marital home or worked without her husband's consent, subject to exceptions. Authorities also prosecuted women social-media influencers under vague morality charges, including a two-year prison sentence and fine imposed on Salma al-Shimy.","question_ids":["3B.7","4B.7","6B.3","6B.8","7B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The policies and prosecution were reported during 2023; the statutory rule may predate the period.","ruler_attribution":"The law and prosecutions are attributed to Egyptian institutions; personal authorship or intervention by Sisi is not established.","limitations":["The statutory framework predates 2023.","The source does not quantify the number of women affected."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d886e5b208764c0a","start_unit":8,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch documented 29 cases involving arrests and prosecutions of LGBT people, including foreigners, and reported a coordinated policy either directed or acquiesced to by senior officials. Reported abuses in detention included solitary confinement, denial of food, water, family contact, and medical services, sexual assault, and other physical violence.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.3","3B.7","3B.10","4B.7","6B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The cases and report were documented during 2023, with some conduct occurring over preceding years.","ruler_attribution":"The source suggests direction or acquiescence by senior government officials but does not prove Sisi's personal authorization.","limitations":["The report documents 29 cases, not necessarily the total population affected.","The claim of a coordinated policy is an inference from the documented cases."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d886e5b208764c0a","start_unit":8,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"In June 2023, Egypt required all Sudanese nationals to obtain visas, making it more difficult for women, children, and older people previously exempt from visa requirements to flee the Sudan conflict. By September, Egypt had received more than 317,000 refugees, including 310,000 Sudanese.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.4","2B.10","3B.7","3B.9","6B.6","6B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The visa decision occurred in June 2023 and the refugee count was reported as of September 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The decision is attributed to the Egyptian government; the source does not identify Sisi's personal role in issuing it.","limitations":["The refugee-hosting figure is attributed to UNHCR via HRW.","The excerpt does not quantify processing outcomes or assistance quality."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d886e5b208764c0a","start_unit":9,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"The US waived human-rights conditions for $235 million of Egypt's $300 million in annual military assistance for fiscal year 2022, withholding $85 million because of insufficient progress on political prisoners, due process, and intimidation of American citizens. The European Parliament adopted an October urgency resolution urging Egypt to end repression ahead of the presidential elections.","question_ids":["2B.5","3B.5","4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The US announcement and European Parliament resolution occurred in September and October 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern Egypt's government under Sisi; the foreign governments' decisions are external responses rather than Sisi actions.","limitations":["The military-aid decision involved US policy and does not itself establish the extent of Egyptian compliance.","The excerpt does not report Sisi's response to the resolution."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The source is a Human Rights Watch country report summarizing events and institutional findings; it does not provide direct access to Egyptian government records or establish personal responsibility by Sisi for every action attributed to state authorities.","No source material supplied facts specifically relevant to nuclear weapons, nuclear command and control, proliferation controls, or AI, cyber, biological, and other catastrophic dual-use safeguards beyond the reported child-data exposure."]}
